args.body:
REDLINE REVIEW MEMORANDUM
Investment Advisory Agreement — Counterparty Markup Analysis
Practice Area: Funds / Asset Management
Matter File 15 — Funds Asset Management
Output: redline-review-memorandum.docx

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

This memorandum reviews the counterparty's redline of the firm-standard Investment Advisory Agreement against (i) the base deal materials, (ii) the disclosure schedules and exhibits (which control over general statements in the base materials), and (iii) the controlling deal-team instruction reflected in the latest partner correspondence.

The counterparty accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces three material deviations:

  (1) Indemnification — silent reduction of the indemnification cap, and conversion of the indemnification basket from a deductible to a tipping (first-dollar) basket;
  (2) Material Adverse Effect — new carve-outs for regulatory action of the type already at issue on this engagement; and
  (3) Survival / limitation period — a shortened survival period for the core representations, which contradicts the survival matrix in Exhibit B.

Reconciliation with the schedules and the controlling client instruction yields the following disposition:

  • Basket conversion (deductible → tipping): ACCEPT / CONCEDE per controlling partner instruction.
  • Indemnification cap reduction: REJECT; restore firm-standard cap; reconcile against Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities.
  • MAE regulatory-action carve-outs: REJECT (or narrowly counter); Schedule 3.7 pending inquiries make these carve-outs especially adverse.
  • Survival-period reduction: REJECT — WALK-AWAY ISSUE per controlling partner instruction; restore Exhibit B survival matrix.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
II. MATERIALS REVIEWED AND SCOPE
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Operative materials (relied upon):

  • Deal materials — funds-asset-management analyze: Analyze Counterparty Markup of Investment Advisory Agreement (Matter File 15 base materials) — standard-form IAA framework covering representations and warranties, covenants, conditions to closing, indemnification, and termination.
  • Counterparty markup — funds-asset-management (counterparty redline identifying the three deviation clusters described above).
  • Schedules and exhibits — funds-asset-management:
      – Schedule 3.7 (pending regulatory inquiries);
      – Schedule 5.2 (retained liabilities);
      – Exhibit B (survival matrix).
    Scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the base materials.
  • Deal correspondence — funds-asset-management (partner email thread). The latest message revises analysis priorities and is controlling: client will concede the basket conversion; any survival-period reduction is a walk-away issue. Earlier messages stating the opposite priority ordering are superseded and are not relied upon.

Excluded:

  • Unrelated / misfiled administrative correspondence in the matter folder (distractor file). Contents concern a different client engagement and have not been used.

Standard of review: each counterparty deviation is tested against firm-standard form and internal funds/asset-management playbook expectations, then reconciled to the schedules/exhibits and the controlling client instruction, with an Accept / Reject / Counter recommendation and negotiation posture.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
III. DEVIATION-BY-DEVIATION ANALYSIS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
DEVIATION 1 — INDEMNIFICATION: CAP REDUCTION AND BASKET CONVERSION
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

A. Counterparty change

  The markup (i) silently reduces the indemnification cap below the firm-standard level and (ii) converts the indemnification basket from a deductible basket to a tipping (first-dollar / threshold-then-tipping) basket.

B. Base-form / playbook position

  Firm-standard Investment Advisory Agreement indemnification architecture for this product:

  • Cap: set at the firm-standard level calibrated to advisory-fee economics and residual operational risk retained by the adviser / sponsor side under the IAA structure. Silent reduction is inconsistent with playbook and with fee-for-risk allocation customary on comparable mandates.
  • Basket: deductible basket — losses below the basket are borne by the indemnified party and do not count toward the cap once the basket is exceeded; the deductible structure is the firm default for ordinary (non-fundamental) indemnity claims under advisory agreements of this type.

C. Schedule interaction (Schedule 5.2) — mandatory reconciliation

  Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities. Those scheduled retained liabilities narrow the corresponding representation and allocate specified residual exposures to the party retaining them under the base deal.

  Effect of the markup if accepted without conforming edits:

  • Cap reduction would silently shrink the recoverable pool available for indemnity claims that arise from or relate to exposures adjacent to Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities, shifting economic risk that the base materials and Schedule 5.2 allocated differently.
  • Basket conversion (addressed below under client instruction) changes the attachment point and recovery economics but does not, by itself, rewrite Schedule 5.2. The cap reduction, however, interacts directly with Schedule 5.2 by reducing headroom for claims that sit outside pure retained-liability carve-outs but are commercially linked to the same risk clusters.

  Playbook rule applied: scheduled exceptions control over general base-form statements; any indemnification redesign must be stress-tested against Schedule 5.2 so that retained-liability allocations are not inverted by a silent cap cut.

D. Client instruction

  Controlling partner correspondence: the client will concede the basket conversion (deductible → tipping). The correspondence does not authorize concession on the cap reduction. Cap reduction remains a live issue for rejection or counter.

E. Recommendation

  1. Basket conversion (deductible → tipping basket): ACCEPT / CONCEDE, expressly pursuant to the controlling client instruction. Document the concession in the issues list and in the revised draft so it is not re-opened without authority.
  2. Indemnification cap reduction: REJECT. Restore the firm-standard cap.
     Counter (if commercially needed to close): any modest cap movement must be (a) overt (not silent), (b) paired with express preservation of recovery for claims tied to Schedule 5.2-adjacent exposures, and (c) subject to the usual carve-outs from the cap for fraud, willful misconduct, and fundamental representations (including advisory-authority, registration/status, and fee-calculation fundamentals customary for IAAs).
  3. Conforming edits: revise the indemnification section and any related definitions so that Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities continue to operate as scheduled and are not re-allocated by the cap language. Add a short schedule-priority clause if not already present confirming that Schedule 5.2 controls in the event of conflict with general indemnity limitations.

F. Negotiation posture

  Lead with restoration of the firm cap; treat basket concession as already authorized client give. Do not trade survival (Deviation 3) for further indemnity give.

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
DEVIATION 2 — MATERIAL ADVERSE EFFECT: REGULATORY-ACTION CARVE-OUTS
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

A. Counterparty change

  The definition of Material Adverse Effect is revised to add carve-outs for regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue on this matter. As revised, events, changes, or effects arising from or relating to such regulatory action would be excluded from MAE, narrowing the buyer's / client's MAE walk right and related bring-down and termination protections.

B. Base-form / playbook position

  Firm-standard MAE for investment-advisory / funds-asset-management IAAs:

  • MAE is a client-protective closing and termination condition, with customary carve-outs (general market, industry-wide, changes in law of general application, etc.) that are balanced and do not erase deal-specific regulatory risk.
  • Playbook disfavors target- or counterparty-driven carve-outs that exclude the precise regulatory risk profile of the engagement, particularly where disclosure already surfaces pending regulatory matters.

C. Schedule interaction (Schedule 3.7) — mandatory reconciliation

  Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries. Those inquiries intersect the markup's new MAE regulatory-action carve-outs.

  Combined effect if the markup is accepted:

  • The two pending inquiries are already on schedule (so they qualify the corresponding representation and limit claim theories that depend on non-disclosure).
  • The new MAE carve-outs would go further: even if those inquiries (or related regulatory action of the same kind) ripen into a material adverse development between signing and closing or during a relevant bring-down window, the MAE condition would not be available.
  • Net result: Schedule 3.7 plus the MAE carve-outs would leave the client with disclosure of the risk but without the principal contractual tool (MAE) to exit or reprice if that disclosed regulatory risk materializes adversely — a classic "disclosed and carved out" double hit that firm playbook rejects for core regulatory exposures on advisory mandates.

  Playbook rule applied: scheduled regulatory exceptions control the representation baseline; they do not justify expanding MAE carve-outs to nullify MAE protection for the same risk cluster. Disclosure ≠ MAE exclusion.

D. Client instruction

  Controlling correspondence does not direct concession on MAE. MAE regulatory carve-outs remain fully negotiable and should be resisted.

E. Recommendation

  REJECT the new regulatory-action carve-outs in the MAE definition, or, if a limited counter is required for deal dynamics:

  • Counter Option A (preferred): delete the new regulatory-action carve-outs entirely; retain only firm-standard MAE carve-outs.
  • Counter Option B (narrow fall-back): permit a carve-out solely for industry-wide regulatory changes of general application that do not disproportionately affect the adviser / the account / the strategy, with an express disproportionate-impact add-back; expressly exclude from any carve-out (i) the pending inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7, (ii) any expansion, adverse finding, sanction, limitation on activities, or enforcement action arising out of or relating to those inquiries, and (iii) entity-specific or strategy-specific regulatory action.
  • Conforming edits: cross-reference Schedule 3.7 in the MAE definition or in a related interpretation clause so it is unambiguous that Schedule 3.7 matters remain MAE-eligible.

F. Negotiation posture

  High priority. Tie rejection expressly to Schedule 3.7. Do not accept "market MAE" rhetoric that ignores the scheduled inquiries. Escalate if counterparty insists on carving out Schedule 3.7-type regulatory action.

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
DEVIATION 3 — SURVIVAL / LIMITATION PERIOD FOR CORE REPRESENTATIONS
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

A. Counterparty change

  A new limitation period shortens survival for the core representations relative to the firm-standard and relative to the deal's own survival matrix.

B. Base-form / playbook position

  Firm-standard IAA survival architecture:

  • Core / fundamental representations (including those going to authority, due authorization, advisory registration and status, conflicts/affiliation fundamentals, and fee and authority-to-debit mechanics, as applicable to this form) survive for the period set in the firm matrix — typically longer than ordinary operating representations, and in many constructs for the applicable statute of limitations or a multi-year structured period.
  • Ordinary representations survive for a shorter defined period.
  • Playbook treats unauthorized compression of core-rep survival as a material risk transfer and, on this engagement, as a client walk-away item.

C. Exhibit interaction (Exhibit B) — mandatory reconciliation

  Exhibit B sets the survival matrix for the agreement. The markup's limitation-period change contradicts Exhibit B.

  Effect if markup is accepted without conforming Exhibit B:

  • Internal inconsistency between body text and Exhibit B, creating ambiguity over which period governs.
  • Even if body text is treated as controlling, the shortened period undercuts the bargained survival structure memorialized in Exhibit B for core representations.
  • Claims that would have remained live under Exhibit B (including claims linked to risks partially qualified by Schedule 3.7 and Schedule 5.2) may expire before discovery or assertion is practical — especially regulatory and retained-liability adjacent claims that often surface on a longer fuse.

  Playbook rule applied: Exhibit B controls the survival matrix; body-text limitation periods must conform to Exhibit B, not silently override it. Any negotiated change to survival must be made in Exhibit B and in the body concurrently.

D. Client instruction — CONTROLLING / WALK-AWAY

  Latest partner correspondence (controlling over earlier messages in the same thread): the client treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue.

  Earlier messages in the thread stated the opposite priority ordering; those are superseded. This memorandum follows only the latest controlling instruction.

E. Recommendation

  REJECT in full. Restore the survival periods set forth in Exhibit B for all core representations. Make no concession on shortening core-rep survival.

  Required conforming steps if any non-core ordinary-rep timing is later discussed (not authorized as a give on core reps):

  • Edit body limitation-period language to match Exhibit B exactly for core representations.
  • If Exhibit B requires technical clean-up for clarity, revise Exhibit B and body together; do not allow body-only overrides.
  • Preserve customary tolling for pending claims asserted in good faith before expiry and for fraud / intentional misrepresentation (often non-survivable limits or SOL-based).

F. Negotiation posture

  Non-negotiable / walk-away per client. Do not trade Deviation 3 against basket concession (already given) or against MAE or cap points. If counterparty maintains the shortened core-rep survival, escalate to partner / client for walk-away confirmation rather than split the difference.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
IV. CROSS-CUTTING RECONCILIATION (MARKUP × SCHEDULES × CLIENT INSTRUCTION)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The three deviations are not independent. They must be read together with the schedules:

  1. Schedule 3.7 (two pending regulatory inquiries)
     × MAE regulatory carve-outs (Deviation 2)
     × shortened survival (Deviation 3)
     → If both Deviation 2 and Deviation 3 were accepted, the client would face disclosed regulatory risk, no MAE exit if it worsens, and a truncated post-closing claim window — an unacceptable cumulative shift.

  2. Schedule 5.2 (retained liabilities)
     × indemnification cap reduction (Deviation 1)
     × shortened survival (Deviation 3)
     → Cap cut reduces recoverable dollars; shorter survival reduces time to recover. Together they re-trade Schedule 5.2's carefully drawn retained-liability boundary.

  3. Exhibit B (survival matrix)
     × Deviation 3 body-text limitation period
     → Direct contradiction; Exhibit B must be restored as controlling.

  4. Client instruction overlay
     • Basket conversion: authorized concede.
     • Survival reduction: walk-away — overrides any impulse to "package" survival with other gives.
     • Cap and MAE: no authorized concede; reject / counter as above.

Cumulative recommendation: accept only the basket conversion; reject cap reduction, MAE regulatory carve-outs, and survival shortening; conform all body text to Schedule 3.7, Schedule 5.2, and Exhibit B.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
V. PROVISIONS ACCEPTED / NOT IN DISPUTE
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The counterparty's revision accepts most firm-standard provisions outside the three deviation clusters. No other deviations are identified in the counterparty markup materials. Unless a further markup round introduces new changes, the remainder of the firm-standard IAA (including standard representations and warranties framework, covenants, conditions to closing, and termination architecture, as qualified by the schedules) may proceed on firm form, subject to ordinary clean-up and schedule consistency review at the next draft turn.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
VI. ACTION LIST AND DRAFTING DIRECTIVES
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Immediate drafting / negotiation actions:

  [ ] 1. Indemnification — Basket: implement tipping-basket language per client concession; note concession on issues list with authority citation to latest partner instruction.
  [ ] 2. Indemnification — Cap: restore firm-standard cap; remove silent reduction; add/confirm cap carve-outs for fraud, willful misconduct, and fundamental reps.
  [ ] 3. Indemnification — Schedule 5.2: insert or confirm schedule-priority language so retained liabilities on Schedule 5.2 are not shifted by indemnity limitations; run a line-by-line check that cap restoration preserves recovery economics around Schedule 5.2 items.
  [ ] 4. MAE definition: delete counterparty regulatory-action carve-outs (or implement Counter Option B disproportionate-impact formulation with express Schedule 3.7 carve-in); confirm firm-standard MAE carve-out set only.
  [ ] 5. Survival: delete shortened limitation period for core representations; conform body text to Exhibit B survival matrix in full; confirm tolling and fraud/intentional-misrep treatment.
  [ ] 6. Exhibit B: verify matrix unchanged and controlling; if any ordinary-rep timing is later negotiated, revise Exhibit B and body together.
  [ ] 7. Consistency pass: definitions, bring-down conditions, termination rights, and indemnity claim procedures must reflect the MAE and survival restorations.
  [ ] 8. Issues list / cover email: flag survival as walk-away; flag MAE/Schedule 3.7 and cap/Schedule 5.2 as reject-with-narrow-counter only; confirm basket as client give.
  [ ] 9. Do not rely on or cite the misfiled unrelated administrative correspondence in the matter folder.

Responsible posture for next markup turn: return a firm draft implementing items 1–7, accompanied by a short issues list reflecting Section III recommendations and the controlling client instruction.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
VII. DISPOSITION TABLE (SUMMARY)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Item                                 | Source conflict                         | Client instruction        | Disposition
-------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|---------------------------|---------------------------
Indemnification basket               | Deductible (firm) → tipping (CP)        | Concede basket conversion | ACCEPT / CONCEDE
Indemnification cap                  | Silent reduction vs firm cap;           | No concede                | REJECT; restore firm cap;
                                     | Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities       |                           | conform to Sch. 5.2
MAE — regulatory-action carve-outs   | New CP carve-outs vs firm MAE;          | No concede                | REJECT (or narrow counter
                                     | Schedule 3.7 pending inquiries          |                           | preserving Sch. 3.7)
Survival / limitation (core reps)    | Shortened period vs Exhibit B matrix    | WALK-AWAY if reduced      | REJECT; restore Exhibit B
Other firm-standard provisions       | Accepted by CP                          | n/a                       | ACCEPT (no change)

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
VIII. CLOSING
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The counterparty markup is largely on firm form but the three identified deviations — particularly when read with Schedule 3.7, Schedule 5.2, and Exhibit B — would materially reallocate regulatory and indemnification risk and compress post-closing remedies. Per the controlling partner instruction, concede only the basket conversion; treat any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue; reject the silent indemnification cap reduction and the MAE regulatory-action carve-outs, with conforming restoration to the schedules and Exhibit B.

This memorandum is the comprehensive redline review deliverable requested for this funds asset management engagement (Output: redline-review-memorandum.docx).

— End of Memorandum —
